title: P0 Hotfix - allocator bridging and soft-resurrected KV handles triggering intermittent GPU OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Several customers reported recurring, hard-to-reproduce GPU OOMs over the past 48 hours affecting mixed short/long token workloads. Incidents surfaced on Hosted during burst traffic and on Dedicated/Private under steady-state heavy multi-tenant shadow loads. Investigation revealed a subtle interaction between the allocator 'bridging' path and KV cache lifecycle (soft-deletes). When a KV handle was freed concurrently with mid-flight prefix cache lookups, the allocator sometimes revalidated and 'resurrected' a tombstoned entry into an ephemeral index slot. That resurrected state caused repeated small allocations and deallocations within the same arena, producing rapid fragmentation and slab splits. On GPUs with constrained device memory the fragmentation manifested as OOMs even while global usage was below absolute capacity.
root_cause: Allocator bridging code path attempted to rebind soft-freed KV entries under certain races (concurrent lookup + background cache compaction). The rebind created transient handle chains that prevented timely coalescing of freed blocks in the arena; combined with workload-driven allocation hot spots this escalated into slab splintering and device OOM.
mitigation: 1) Immediate rate-limit and backpressure on affected Hosted routes (applied by routing team) 2) Scoped heap pressure throttle on Dedicated pools 3) Patch release for Private customers with instructions to enable progressive compaction. All customers advised to reduce long-tail concurrent prefix lookups as temporary measure.
fix_summary: Backported hotfix changes: (A) stop resurrect-on-lookup semantics — once a KV handle is tombstoned it is logically immutable until compaction finishes, (B) add a bounded background compaction worker with exponential backoff to smooth arena reclamation, (C) introduce a small device->host spill window to give critical ops breathing room on GPUs under high fragmentation, (D) add assert/fuzz tests for the allocator-KV race.
qa_checks:
- deterministic multi-threaded allocator replay harness reproducer added to CI
- 72-hour soak on canary nodes with mixed short/long token profiles
- GPU memory fragmentation metrics (free-run variance) gated for rollout
- unit tests for tombstone lifecycle and rebind prevention
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Canary 1% Hosted (runtime-1.27.4-hotfix) for 4h observation
Phase 2: Canary ramp to 10% for 12h with alerting thresholds
Phase 3: Full hosted roll after 24h stable
Dedicated: scheduled maintenance window with hotpatch applied and node drains (customers notified)
Private: package and release with upgrade runbook; offer onsite assist for high-risk customers
rollback_plan: If fragmentation or new allocation regressions observed, disable bounded compactor and revert allocator bridge change immediately; enable emergency host-spill to avoid OOM while rollback proceeds. Rollback script provided in PR and incident runbook.
customer_notes:
- Customer: Acme Health (Dedicated) reported 5 incidents, supplied traces and core dumps.
- Customer: NovaChat (Hosted) spike during nightly batch exposed issue.
- Enterprise partner: GovData (Private) requested patched bundle and manual install checklist.
